newsitem.title: USA: Tandy to shut McDuff stores, take charge.
newsitem.headline: Tandy to shut McDuff stores, take charge.

text.p: Tandy Corp. said Tuesday it plans to close its chain of 53 McDuff electronic stores in Texas and the Southeast and take a charge of at least $20 million in the fourth quarter.

Ft. Worth, Tex.-based Tandy, which operates nearly 6,930 stores under the Radio Shack, Computer City and Incredible Universe names, cited losses at the McDuff outlets due to stiff competition in the retail electronics industry.

It also said in a statement that the units no longer fit into its long-term plan. Radio Shack said on Monday that its plans to add about 100 company-owned and operated stores each year through 1999 were ahead of schedule.

Most of the McDuff stores, which sell consumer electronics products and appliances, are located in Texas and Florida, with others in Tennessee, Georgia, Mississippi, Alabama and Oklahoma, Tandy Investor Relations Director Martin Moad said.
Some of the 450 to 500 employees who work at McDuff will be transferred to other Tandy operations and some will lose their jobs, he said but declined to cite specific figures.
The stores will be closed after the holidays, he said.
Merchandise will be liquidated in coming weeks and warranties and service contracts on merchandise previously sold at McDuff will be honoured, the company said.
Tandy stock fell 25 cents to $42.25 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
